Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis. Keep a claim-to-source mapping through every step, annotate conflicts instead of choosing a number, require dates so time differences are not mistaken for contradictions, and present each kind of content in its natural format.
What you need to know

Each time findings are summarised, it is tempting to drop the sources "to save space". By the final report, claims stand without citations. The fix is structural: every subagent outputs claim-source mappings , and every downstream step must preserve and merge them. {"claim": "EU e-bike sales rose 12% in 2025", "source": "European Cycling Industry Report 2026", "url": "https://example.org/eci-2026", "excerpt": "sales increased by 12 percent year on year", "published": "2026-02-18", "method": "survey of 40 manufacturers"}

docs.h: Conflicting figures: annotate, do not choose
docs.x: Two credible sources give different market sizes: $12.4 billion (January 2026) and $8.7 billion (March 2025). Picking one silently, or averaging them, hides a real disagreement. Report both, with their sources , and let the reader or the coordinator decide. Document analysis should finish with the conflicting values included and annotated ; the coordinator decides how to reconcile them before synthesis.

Many apparent conflicts are time differences : a 2025 figure and a 2026 figure for a growing market both being correct. Require publication or data-collection dates in every structured output so synthesis can tell "contradiction" from "change over time".

- Separate well-established findings (several independent sources) from contested ones. - Keep the original characterisation : if a source said "estimated" or "preliminary", say so. - Keep methodological context (survey size, sample, model) where it affects interpretation.

docs.h: Use the right format for each content type
docs.c: Every claim keeps its source and date · Picking the most recent figure
docs.x: Content Format Financial data Tables News and events Prose Technical findings Structured lists Converting everything to uniform paragraphs makes figures hard to compare and technical detail hard to scan. From the first subagent to the final report, no step may drop them. "Use the newer number" sounds reasonable but discards a credible source without telling the reader. Annotate both.
Scenario 3: reports with no citations, conflicting statistics, figures from different years, and uniform prose for mixed content.
Check your understanding

Whitfield's citations disappear and conflicting figures are quietly resolved. Write the provenance rules. 1. Define the finding record every subagent returns. 2. Write the conflict rule for document analysis and the coordinator. 3. Lay out the report sections that separate established and contested findings. 4. Choose formats for the market-size data, regulatory news and technical battery findings. 1. Finding record. claim, source name, URL or document name, page or section, excerpt, published or collected date, method note, and which subagent produced it. 2. Conflict rule. Document analysis never resolves conflicts: it returns every value with its record and sets conflict: true on the group. The coordinator then checks dates (time difference or disagreement?) and method notes, and passes the annotated group to synthesis, which must show all values. 3. Sections. Summary; Established findings (two or more independent sources); Contested findings (each with the competing values and their sources); Coverage and gaps; Sources. 4. Formats. Market size: a table with value, year, source and method. Regulatory news: short dated prose. Battery findings: a structured list (chemistry, energy density, cost per kWh, source). - Every finding carries source, excerpt and date. - Conflicts are annotated, never silently resolved. - Established and contested findings are separate. - Each content type has its own format.

docs.h: How to read a CCAR-F question
docs.x: Most items describe a production system with one flaw and ask for the best fix. Five habits pick the right option: 1. "Must always" or "must never" means code. A hook, a gate or a permission, never a louder prompt. 2. Fix the layer that failed. Missing subtopics are a coordinator decomposition problem, not a search problem. 3. Prefer the targeted fix. A bigger model, a larger context window or temperature 0 is almost never the answer. 4. Never hide a failure. An error is not an empty result, and a timeout is not "no data". 5. Ask instead of guessing. Two matching customers means ask for an identifier.

stop_reason What the loop does tool_use Run every requested tool, append the results, call Claude again end_turn Stop; the last response is the answer max_tokens Incomplete: continue or raise the limit, never present it as done stop_sequence Treat as end of turn unless that sequence means something to you - The loop ends on stop_reason , not on text content, "I'm done" phrases or an iteration cap. A cap is a safety net only. Tool results are never fed back automatically: your code appends them. 1.1 - The coordinator is the only hub. It decomposes, picks only the subagents a query needs, routes every message and loops back when the synthesis has gaps. Subagents never talk to each other. 1.2 - Subagents start with no memory. Everything they need goes in their prompt: complete findings, paths, constraints, with structured metadata so citations survive. Spawn them in parallel in one turn. Give goals and quality criteria, not step-by-step scripts. 1.3 - A coordinator that never delegates is missing the Task tool in allowedTools . The guide says Task ; current SDK releases call it Agent . Answer with Task. 1.3 - Multi-issue messages: decompose and resolve each item. Several issues is not a reason to escalate. 1.4 - Handoff summary: customer and how verified, the issue in one line, root cause, amounts and orders, actions already taken, why escalated, recommended action. 1.4 Hook Runs Use it to PreToolUse After Claude requests a tool, before it runs Block, redirect or rewrite a call (refund limit, identity first) PostToolUse After the tool runs, before Claude sees the result Normalise formats, trim fields, add context - "CRITICAL" in a tool description and temperature 0 are not guarantees. 1.5 - Decomposition: steps known in advance means a fixed chain; open-ended work means an adaptive plan; a many-file review means per-file passes plus an integration pass. 1.6 - Sessions: resume by name ( --resume ) when the context is still true and say what changed; fork to try two approaches from one analysis; start fresh with a structured summary when most files have changed. 1.7

- A tool description states what it does, its inputs and their format, what it returns, when to use it, when not to (name the neighbour) and edge cases. Fix misrouting in descriptions, names or a split, not with system-prompt examples, and not by merging tools behind a mode flag. 2.1 Error category Example Right response Transient Timeout, service down Retry, perhaps after a wait Validation Wrong order-number format Fix the input or ask the user Business Outside the 45-day window Do not retry; explain the policy Permission Agent may not see payroll Do not retry; escalate or explain - Return failures with the isError flag , a category, a retryable flag and a plain description. A failed search and an empty search are different results. 2.2 tool_choice Effect Use when auto May call a tool or reply in text Conversational default any Must call a tool, chooses which Structured output, several possible schemas {"type": "tool", "name": ...} Must call that tool One step must run first - Tools follow the role: the smallest set per agent, one narrow cross-role tool for a frequent need, constrained tools instead of open-ended ones. 2.3 - MCP scope: shared servers in the project's .mcp.json (committed), personal ones in ~/.claude.json , secrets as ${VAR} , never a literal token. If Claude prefers Grep over a capable MCP tool, improve the MCP tool's description; do not disable Grep. Expose catalogues as resources. 2.4 - Built-in tools: Grep searches file contents , Glob matches file paths ( / .test.tsx ), Edit changes text by a unique match (fall back to Read plus Write), Bash runs commands. Grep first, then read selectively. 2.5

CLAUDE.md level Location Shared? User ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md No, you only Project CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md at the repo root Yes, via version control Directory CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory Yes, if committed - Team standards go in the project file or .claude/rules/ ; split big files with @import ; check what loaded with /memory . One-off context stays in the conversation. Hard rules go in hooks or permissions. 3.1 - Commands and skills: shared in .claude/commands/ and .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md ; personal in the same paths under ~/.claude/ . Frontmatter: context: fork runs it in an isolated sub-agent (for noisy output), allowed-tools limits its tools, argument-hint prompts for a parameter. Skills load on demand; CLAUDE.md loads always. 3.2 - Path rules: a file in .claude/rules/ with paths: [" / .test.ts"] loads only for matching files. Use it for conventions that follow a file type across the tree, not one CLAUDE.md per folder. 3.3 - Plan mode for wide, unclear or architectural work (migrations, 45+ files, several valid approaches); direct execution for a clear, narrow fix. Send verbose discovery to the Explore subagent. 3.4 - Refinement: concrete input and output examples for inconsistent transformations, tests for edge cases, let Claude interview you in an unfamiliar domain, interacting bugs in one message, independent ones one at a time. 3.5 - CI: -p ( --print ) for non-interactive runs (a hanging job needs -p , not a timeout); --output-format json with --json-schema for parseable findings; context in CLAUDE.md; pass prior findings to stop duplicate comments and existing tests to stop duplicate tests; review with a separate instance. 3.6

- Precision comes from categories, not confidence. Say what to report and what to skip, and define each severity with an example. "Be conservative" does nothing measurable. Switch off a noisy category while you fix it. 4.1 - Few-shot: two to four examples aimed at the ambiguous cases, each with its reason and the exact output format, matching the real input type. 4.2 - Structured output: define a tool whose input schema is your JSON schema, require it with tool_choice , read the tool_use block. Make absent fields nullable (required fields invite invention); use enums with an "other" or "unclear" value. The schema guarantees structure, not truth. 4.3 - Validation and retry: check meaning (line items sum to the total, fields in the right place). Retry with the document, the failed output and the exact errors. If the information is not in the document, stop retrying. 4.4 Messages API Message Batches API Cost Standard About 50% less Results Seconds Within 24 hours, no latency SLA Tools mid-request Yes No - Batch only what nobody waits for (overnight reports, backlogs), never a pre-merge check. Match results by custom_id and resubmit only the failures. 4.5 - Review with an independent instance. Same-session self-review rarely catches its own bug, even with more thinking. Have findings carry confidence for routing. 4.6

- Long conversations: keep amounts, dates, IDs and promises in a persistent case-facts block, not in summarised prose. Trim verbose tool results. Put key findings first, since the middle of long input gets less attention. A bigger window is not the fix. 5.1 Escalate Do not escalate for The customer asks for a human (escalate immediately ) Negative sentiment alone Policy is silent or ambiguous (such as competitor price matching) A self-reported confidence score No meaningful progress is possible Several issues in one message - Several matching records: ask for an identifier; never pick the most likely. 5.2 - Error propagation: retry transient errors locally; report the rest with failure type, what was attempted, partial results and alternatives. Never return an empty success, and never abort the whole run for one failure. 5.3 - Long explorations: a scratchpad file for findings, subagents for noisy questions, summaries between phases, /compact , and state exports with a manifest for crash recovery. 5.4 - Human review: an overall accuracy figure hides weak segments. Check accuracy by document type and field, keep sampling high-confidence output, calibrate confidence on labelled data, and route reviewers to likely errors. 5.5 - Provenance: every claim keeps its source and date through every step. Show conflicting figures side by side with both sources; do not pick the newer one. Tables for financial data, prose for news, lists for technical findings. 5.6

Type Share Notes Invoices 70% Hundreds of layouts; some handwritten; some from international suppliers Receipts 15% Photos and scans, often low quality Contracts 10% 5 to 80 pages; payment terms buried in clauses Other 5% Credit notes, statements, cover letters, things nobody expected

- A prompt says "respond with JSON". About 4% of responses fail to parse (markdown fences, trailing commas, extra prose). - The schema marks vendor_tax_id as required.
